prompt:
In the `Lifecycle` demo, *15 more* is clicked once. What do `onBeforeUpdate` and `onUpdated` read from the `

`?
hint: The two hooks sit on either side of one redraw.

choices.text: 45 in both, since the ref had already changed
choices.why: The ref had changed, but the hooks read the page, and before the redraw the page still said 30.

choices.text: Nothing in `onBeforeUpdate`; the element is rebuilt
choices.why:
The redraw patches the same `

`. The transcript reads 30 and 45 from one element.

choices.text: 30 before the redraw and then 45 after it, read from one element
choices.why: Right. `onBeforeUpdate` runs before the redraw and sees the old value; `onUpdated` runs after it and sees the new one.

choices.text: 30 in both, as the page redraws once every hook is done

prompt: In a `<script setup>` component, where does the code go that Vue 2 put in the `created` hook?
hint: Look for the hook the lesson says does not exist.

choices.text: In `onBeforeMount`, the first hook Vue calls
choices.why: `onBeforeMount` comes after setup, so it is later than `created` was.

choices.text: In `onCreated`, imported from `vue` like the others
choices.why: There is no `onCreated` in the Composition API.

choices.text: In `onMounted`, once the component exists on the page
choices.why: That is later still: the component has been created and inserted by then.

choices.text: At the top level of `<script setup>`, which is creation
choices.why: Right. Setup itself is creation, so its top level runs where `created` ran.

prompt: A component hands an element to a chart library. On removal the library must be told `chart.destroy()`, and that call reads the element. Which hook should make it?
hint: Which hook still has the elements?

choices.text: `onBeforeUnmount`
choices.why: Right. The elements are still there and still working, so the library is able to let go of its own.

choices.text: `onUnmounted`, where everything a component started is stopped
choices.why: That is the place for a timer. By then the elements are gone, and `destroy()` needs one.

choices.text: `onUpdated`, after the last redraw
choices.why: A removal is not a redraw of the component, and `onUpdated` does not run for it.

choices.text: A watcher with `flush: 'post'` on the chart's data
choices.why: A watcher runs when a value changes. Removal changes no value of the chart's.

prompt: Code that runs after one value changes and needs the page is a watcher with `flush: '___'`, rather than `onUpdated`.
hint: Lesson 4 set it, and it is the opposite of *pre*.

prompt: In the `Order` demo, whose `mounted` line is printed last?
hint: Creation goes down; mounting comes back up.

choices.text: The second child's, the last component created
choices.why: It was created last, but the parent's `mounted` waits for both children.

choices.text: The first child's, since mounting runs backwards
choices.why: The children are mounted first to last; what comes back up is the tree, child then parent.

choices.text: The parent's, after both of its children are mounted
choices.why: Right. A parent is mounted after all its children are on the page.

choices.text: Whichever child finished rendering last, which varies
choices.why: The order is fixed by the tree, and the transcript shows it: the two children, then the parent.

prompt: Which of these are true inside a parent's own `onMounted`? Choose all that apply.
hint: In the transcript, what had already been printed when `parent: mounted` appeared?

choices.text: Every child is on the page
choices.why: Right. The parent is mounted only after its children are.

choices.text: The children have not run their setup yet
choices.why: Their setup ran right after the parent's `beforeMount`, long before.

choices.text: A template ref to a child component is filled
choices.why: Right. It is `null` until then, and filled by the time the parent's `onMounted` runs.

choices.text: Each child's `onMounted` has already run
choices.why: Right. Both children's `mounted` lines come before the parent's.

prompt: A parent creates an object in its `onMounted` and puts it where its children read it. A child reads it in its own `onMounted`. What does the child find?
hint: Which `onMounted` runs first, the parent's or the child's?

choices.text: The object, since a parent's hooks all run before its children's
choices.why: That holds for setup and `beforeMount`, not for `mounted`, which comes back up the tree.

choices.text: Nothing yet: its `onMounted` runs before the parent's
choices.why: Right. The fix is to create it in the parent's setup, which runs before any child exists.

choices.text: An error, because a child cannot read from its parent in `onMounted`
choices.why: Reading is allowed; the problem is only the timing. The value is not there yet.

choices.text: The object, because both hooks run at the same moment
choices.why: They run one after the other, children first, as the transcript prints them.

prompt: A parent and its two children are removed together. In whose `onUnmounted` are the others sure to have finished cleaning up?
hint: `unmounted` runs in the opposite direction to `beforeUnmount`.

choices.text: The first child's, as it is the first to go
choices.why: It is the first `unmounted`, so nobody else has finished at that point.

choices.text: Nobody's: Vue does not fix the order
choices.why: It does, and the transcript shows it: children first, then the parent.

choices.text: The second child's, the last child removed
choices.why: The parent's `unmounted` still comes after it.

choices.text: The parent's, the last of the three to be gone
choices.why: Right. Removal starts and finishes at the top, so the parent is the last to be gone.

prompt: What does `minutesField.value` hold right after `adding.value = true`, before `await nextTick()`?
hint: The `v-if` has been told, not redrawn.

choices.text: The `<input>`, since the `v-if` is now true
choices.why: The condition is true, but the redraw is still in the queue.

choices.text: A promise that resolves to the input
choices.why: A template ref holds an element or `null`, never a promise; `nextTick` is the promise here.

choices.text: `null`
choices.why: Right. The element does not exist until the queued redraw runs, which is what `await nextTick()` waits for.

choices.text: An empty array, as the field sits in a list
choices.why: Only a `ref` inside a `v-for` collects an array, and the field is outside the loop.

prompt: Why does the lesson say to look up the elements of a `v-for` ref by something on the element rather than by index?
hint: Compare the array with the list it came from.

choices.text: The array holds component instances, not elements
choices.why: On plain `<li>` elements it holds elements; the demo counted 3 of them.

choices.text: Its order is not guaranteed to match the order of the list
choices.why: Right. Index 0 of the array need not be the first item of the list.

choices.text: The array stays `null` until `nextTick`, so reading an index fails
choices.why: In `onMounted` it already held 3 rows.

choices.text: Every read of the ref builds a new array in a new order
choices.why: The order is unspecified, not reshuffled on each read; the point is that nobody promised it.

prompt: A parent puts `ref="field"` on a child component written with `<script setup>`. Which of the child's functions is the parent able to call through it?
hint: The child decides.

choices.text: Every function declared in the child's script
choices.why: With `<script setup>` the instance is closed: nothing reaches the parent by being declared.

choices.text: Only the ones the child passes to `defineExpose`
choices.why: Right. The child offers a few, like `focus()`, and keeps the rest to itself.

choices.text: None: a ref on a component is always `null`
choices.why: It holds the component's instance; what is reachable on it is what the child exposes.

choices.text: The methods of its root element, such as `focus()` on an input
choices.why: A ref on a component gives the instance, not an element. `focus()` is there only if the child exposes it.

prompt: `Ticker` sets its interval to 100 milliseconds. How many times a second does `careless` go on ticking after it has been removed?
hint: A thousand milliseconds in a second.

prompt: In the `Leak` demo, what happens to the two timers after *Remove both*?
hint: Only one of the two registered `onUnmounted`.

choices.text: Both stop, because Vue clears a component's timers
choices.why: Vue cleans up what Vue created. `setInterval` is the browser's, and nothing stops it but `clearInterval`.

choices.text: Both keep ticking until the page reloads
choices.why: `tidy` called `clearInterval` in its `onUnmounted`, and its lines stop in the transcript.

choices.text: `careless` goes on ticking; `tidy` stops
choices.why: Right. The component is gone from the page and from Vue, and its interval still runs.

choices.text: `careless` stops a moment later, once garbage collection frees it
choices.why: The interval keeps its function reachable, so nothing it holds is ever freed.

prompt: A component is removed. Which of these does Vue stop by itself? Choose all that apply.
hint: Vue cleans up what Vue created.

choices.text: A `ResizeObserver` watching one of its elements
choices.why: The observer is the browser's; it needs `disconnect()`.

choices.text: A watcher made during its setup
choices.why: Right. Watchers made in setup belong to the component and stop with it.

choices.text: A listener it added to `window` in `onMounted`
choices.why: The listener is on `window`, which is not removed; it needs `removeEventListener` with the same function.

choices.text: Its own renders
choices.why: Right. Vue made them and Vue stops them.

choices.text: A `fetch` it started that has not answered
choices.why: The request runs to the end unless an `AbortController` aborts it.

prompt: `App` is removed only when the page closes. Why does the planner still pair its clock with `onUnmounted(() => clearInterval(timer))`?
hint: Where else will these lines run?

choices.text: A browser keeps an interval running after its tab closes
choices.why: Closing the tab ends everything the page started; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Vue warns about an `onMounted` that has no `onUnmounted`
choices.why: Vue has no such warning; the two hooks are independent.

choices.text: A test unmounts `App`, and the lines later move into a composable any component uses
choices.why: Right. In lesson 21's test and in lesson 10's composable, the removal happens and the cleanup matters every time.

choices.text: Without it, `today` would be refreshed twice a minute
choices.why: One `onMounted` starts one interval; the count only grows when the component is mounted again.

prompt: Where does the lesson start a component's request for its data, and why?
hint: Does a request need the page?

choices.text: In `onMounted`, so that it is sent once, as in React
choices.why: Setup already runs once. In React the effect avoids a body that runs on every render, which Vue does not have.

choices.text: In setup: a request needs no page, so it starts sooner
choices.why: Right. It was in flight while Vue rendered and mounted, and answered after both.

choices.text: In `onMounted`, because setup runs again on every redraw
choices.why: That is a React component's body. Vue's setup runs once by construction.

choices.text: In `onBeforeMount`, the last moment before the page exists, so the answer lands in time
choices.why: The lesson does not use it, and it would still start the request later than setup does.

prompt: A component reads `localStorage` at the top level of `<script setup>`. Later the app is rendered on a server. What happens there?
hint: Which of the two runs on the server, setup or `onMounted`?

choices.text: Nothing: setup runs only in the browser
choices.why: It is the other way round. Setup runs on the server too; `onMounted` is what does not.

choices.text: The read fails, since `localStorage` does not exist on the server
choices.why: Right. Setup runs in both places, so that read has to move into `onMounted`.

choices.text: It is skipped on the server, the way `onMounted` is
choices.why: Only the hook is skipped; setup's top level runs.

choices.text: It works, because Nuxt gives the server a `localStorage` of its own
choices.why: Neither `localStorage` nor `window` exists on the server, which is why the planner's reads move.

prompt: On the server, setup runs and `___` does not: there is no page to put the component into.
hint: The hook that waits for the page.

prompt: Inside `<KeepAlive>`, the student switches from Statistics to Spanish. What happens to the statistics component?
hint: Read the line printed right after `-- click #spanish`.

choices.text: It is unmounted, and its note is copied to `localStorage`
choices.why: Nothing writes to `localStorage` here, and the component was not unmounted.

choices.text: It is unmounted and rebuilt on return with the same `:key`
choices.why: Without `<KeepAlive>` that is what happens, and the note comes back empty.

choices.text: It stays mounted and is hidden like `v-show`
choices.why: It is taken off the page; `onDeactivated` is a hook of its own, not a style.

choices.text: It is deactivated and kept in memory, note and all
choices.why: Right. Switching back activated the same instance, and its 5 characters were there.

prompt: A kept component runs a timer that is only useful while the tab is shown. Where does it stop and restart it?
hint: A kept component is not unmounted when it is switched away.

choices.text: `onDeactivated` and `onActivated`
choices.why: Right. Those are the moments it is put away and comes back.

choices.text: `onUnmounted` and `onMounted`, as for any component
choices.why: `onUnmounted` does not run for a kept component until the `<KeepAlive>` itself goes.

choices.text: `onBeforeUpdate` and `onUpdated`, around the switch
choices.why: Switching tabs does not redraw the kept component; it takes it off the page.

choices.text: A watcher on the parent's `tab` ref, inside the child
choices.why: The child does not see the parent's `tab`, and the hooks already say when it is put away.

prompt: Why does the planner not rely on `<KeepAlive>` to hold its sessions?
hint: Where does a kept component live?

choices.text: It keeps at most ten components unless `max` is raised
choices.why: There is no such default; `max` is something you set to limit it.

choices.text: It throws a component's state away at `onDeactivated`
choices.why: The state survives deactivation; the statistics note came back.

choices.text: A reload loses everything that is kept only in memory, kept components included
choices.why: Right. State that must survive anyway goes in `localStorage` or a store.

choices.text: It keeps only the view the student saw most recently
choices.why: It keeps every view it has seen, which is why it trades memory for state.

prompt: A parent with two children is shown and later removed. Put these moments in the order they happen.
hint: Down for creation, back up for mounting; removal starts and ends at the top.

prompt: Match each job to the hook this lesson gives it.
hint: Does the job need the elements, and is it starting or stopping?

pairs.left: measure an element when the component first appears
clear the interval the component started
tell a library to let go of the element it draws in
pause a kept tab's timer while nobody is looking

prompt: A component shown with `v-if` runs `window.addEventListener('resize', () => measure())` in `onMounted` and `window.removeEventListener('resize', () => measure())` in `onUnmounted`. It is shown and hidden 5 times. How many of its resize listeners are left on `window`?
hint: Is the function given to `removeEventListener` the same function?

prompt: A field appears when the student clicks *Edit*, and it must receive the focus. Which of these put the focus in it? Choose all that apply.
hint: The field exists only after the redraw that the click queues.

choices.text: Set the flag, then call `focus()` on the next line
choices.why: The redraw is still queued, so the ref is `null` on that line.

choices.text: Set the flag, `await nextTick()`, then call `focus()`
choices.why: Right. That is the demo's pattern: after the tick the element exists.

choices.text: Call `focus()` in the parent's `onMounted`
choices.why: The parent was mounted long before the click, when the field did not exist.

choices.text: Make the field a component of its own that focuses its input in its `onMounted`
choices.why: Right. Its `onMounted` runs when the `v-if` puts it on the page, which is after the click.
